- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot after spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.40) — model underreacts to downward momentum.
- Lagged corrections: if sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to adjust downward in the next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to revert to 30-day moving average in 10–15 day horizons.
- Overshoot after strong positive sentiment spikes — model forecasts peak too early and then drops too sharply.
- In low sentiment (sentiment < -0.30), model underestimates downside risk and fails to account for volatility clustering.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic when sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +0.20/-0.30).
